chapter: Serenading and playing with Buddy Bolden
title: Serenading groups and strolling bands
summary: Strolling string groups serenaded birthdays and weddings at all hours; Garland says they woke people up and drank the beer.

story.theme_name: Growing up and learning music: family, first instruments, teachers
story.community_name: Where I came from: parents, siblings and birth

blocks.x: Second reel Mr. Garland. So we were talking about a string trio you say?

Yeah. With Eddie? We were talking about Eddie Darcy, yeah. Yeah. We were talking about how we used to run around together playing with the trio, playing mandolin guitar and bass. Nah, he's playing bass violin himself. Playing good bass too.
Well Bro told me he used to play that mandolin around town. What was Bro? Bro, Bro told me he did.
Yeah, I guess they had a lot of groups wandering, strolling, is what I'm talking about. Serenading bands.
I know I played mandolin. I never know if Bro would play on. I can't say he did.
Well that might have been after you left, because you left so early. Mm-hmm. He might have been out in the country when you were here.
Did they have many serenading groups around? Yeah.
Like birthday parties? Yeah, that's what we used to do all the time, serenading. Always go somebody to do all hours a night, serenading. Sure.
What would you do when people got married? Would they have any music or anything?
Some of them would. If we know them, we're going to play music whether we got something or not. We know them. We'd come over and play for them.
Would you wake them up in the middle of the night ever with me?
Oh man, yeah. Oh, we could do that. They was used to that. Sure. Come on, get up, open the door. Come in there and get it. Call the bellboy. Bellboy, bring a can. Get the beer. And we'll have a ball.
Who was rushing those cans then? Did you know any of those?
I thought, didn't Johnny St. Cyr used to work for Frank Early if I remember right?
